citation.title: High-speed data handling using reflective memory thread for tokamak plasma control
citation.authors: S. Y. Park, S. H. Hahn, W. C. Kim, B. G. Penaflor, R. D. Johnson, D. A. Piglowski, M. L. Walker

topic: KSTAR PCS real-time reflective-memory (RFM) thread for exchanging PF coil commands and measurements with magnet power supplies
own_question: How can a dedicated RFM thread move roughly 1 kB of per-cycle I/O within a 50 us control cycle for PF coil feedback?
actual_method_and_evidence: This is an engineering description of the system. The thread copies RFM data into a shared heap by DMA, syncs to the digitizer time counter, and uses a 5 ms timeout and a watchdog. The conclusion states that all RFM data transferred within 50 us, but the supplied text gives no timing distributions. No CES, BES, ECEI, ion temperature or nowcasting content appears.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In KSTAR control, a real-time cycle uses the preceding cycle's measured coil current, which illustrates one-cycle-lagged inputs in feedback.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p.2, Operation of the RFM Thread; Fig. 2 description
claim_checks.qualification: This concerns PF coil current in 2011. It is not about diagnostics or CES report latency.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The 50 us cycle and 5 ms timeout are PF/MPS control facts. They are not CES or BES/ECEI timing and must not be used for our 10 ms grid.
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat this as evidence on CES report arrival times or latency.
Do not claim the KSTAR PCS uses impurity temperature or BES/ECEI data.
Do not cite it as evidence of real-time deployability of our estimator.
Do not transfer the 2011 hardware timings to KSTAR 2022.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: It is generally off-topic. Cite it only if the intro needs a pointer to how KSTAR real-time control infrastructure handles data. Otherwise exclude it.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
